bull_bear.body:
- Experienced management team - stated by the Company as a qualitative factor for the offer price
- Long standing relationships with customers - stated qualitative factor
- Consistent financial performance - stated qualitative factor
- Promoter continuity: Mr. Sudeep Mehta has been integral to the Company since incorporation in 1994 and brings over 30 years of Automotive OEM experience
- Among the few companies with in-line doming application units, enabling high-quality acrylic domed labels for plastic, wood, metal and glass surfaces
- Full quality certification stack for automotive OEM supply - ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018
- Combined manufacturing and trading portfolio spanning both the OEM paint shop and the auto refinish aftermarket
- In-house R&D team plus robust infrastructure with latest precision tools and a well-equipped testing laboratory
- Batch-level quality control - adhesion peel, heat resistance through automotive baking cycles, residue-free removal, tensile strength and elongation, and paint-system compatibility testing
- Customisation offered to meet the diverse requirements of clients
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility and import dependence — Jumbo rolls, solvents, skins, heat film and velcro are global commodities imported from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, USA, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey; raw material cost was 37.01%, 43.26%, 44.29% and 47.10% of total revenues in H1FY26, FY25, FY24 and FY23. Duty changes and price cycles can compress margins where increases cannot be passed through.
- Product concentration in Adhesive Tapes and Die-cuts — A single category contributed 48.13% of revenue in FY25 and 45.00% in the period ended September 30, 2025; a change in OEM masking specification or a substitute technology would hit the largest revenue pool directly.
- Dependence on the automotive OEM and auto refinish cycle — Almost the entire portfolio is tied to vehicle paint shops, body shops and detailing demand, so a downturn in automotive production or refinish volumes flows straight through to revenue.
- Geographic concentration in the domestic market — Exports were 0.53% of revenue in FY25 and 0.64% in the period ended September 30, 2025, leaving effectively no external market to cushion an India demand slowdown.
- Promoter and key-man dependence — Mr. Sudeep Mehta, associated since incorporation in 1994, leads the entire management team and oversees overall management, day-to-day affairs and strategic decision-making.
- Execution risk on the two proposed greenfield units — Both proposed units - RIICO Karoli (Rajasthan) and Model Economic Township, Jhajjar (Haryana) - are to be constructed from Fresh Issue proceeds, and the text available prints no commissioning timeline or added capacity against either.
- Manufacturing concentrated in two locations — All current output comes from Unit I at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur and Unit II at IMT Manesar, with no alternate in-house capacity disclosed to absorb a disruption at either site.
- Foreign exchange and cross-border trade exposure — The Company flags import and export regulations that may erode profit margins or restrict trade, changes in foreign exchange controls and tax rates, and fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates including devaluations, alongside shifts in regional and local economic conditions.

business.body: Sumax Engineering Limited manufactures adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes, domes and graphics and car care products, and additionally trades electrical and pneumatic tools, abrasive sheets/discs/rolls, body shop consumables, retail products and accessories and aerosol products. Products are sold into the automotive OEM paint shop and the auto refinish / body-shop aftermarket, with further application in consumer durables (domed labels for refrigerators, air conditioners, microwaves) and general industrial and hardware use. Manufacturing runs from two units, at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu) and IMT Manesar (Haryana), under ISO and IATF certified processes.

The remaining objects of the Fresh Issue are funding of working capital requirements and general corporate purposes. outlook.body:
- Raw material cost as a share of total revenues has fallen steadily - 47.10% in FY23, 44.29% in FY24, 43.26% in FY25 and 37.01% in the period ended September 30, 2025
- EBITDA margin expanded from 6.32% in FY23 to 8.84% in FY24, 10.21% in FY25 and 11.80% for the period ended September 30, 2025 (margin computed on Total Income)
- PAT margin, on revenue from operations, rose from 3.66% in FY23 to 5.69% in FY24, 6.84% in FY25 and 8.08% in the period ended September 30, 2025
- Revenue growth has been uneven - 35.18% in FY23, 3.13% in FY24 and 11.72% in FY25
- Mix is anchored on Adhesive Tapes and Die-cuts (48.13% of revenue in FY25, 45.00% in the period ended September 30, 2025), with Abrasive Sheets, Discs & Rolls the largest traded line (19.94% in FY25, rising to 24.12% in the period ended September 30, 2025)
- Business is almost entirely domestic - exports were 0.53% of revenue in FY25 and 0.64% in the period ended September 30, 2025
- Balance sheet is lightly levered - debt-equity ratio of 0.15 in FY23, 0.17 in FY24, 0.16 in FY25 and 0.13 as at September 30, 2025
- Return ratios improved through the track record - RoNW 14.75% / 19.11% / 20.42% and RoCE 19.70% / 23.32% / 24.63% for FY23 / FY24 / FY25; the September 30, 2025 figures of 10.60% and 12.89% are half-year and not annualised
- Inputs such as jumbo rolls, solvents, skins, heat film and velcro are sourced from a mix of domestic and foreign suppliers, so input cost is exposed to global commodity cycles, duty changes and currency movement

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Company describes itself as operating both a manufacturing division (adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes, domes and graphics, car care products) and a trading division (tools, abrasives, body shop consumables, retail products, accessories and aerosols), so a portion of what it sells is bought-in rather than made. On the inbound side it is not backward integrated: raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro are sourced from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers, with imports from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, the United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey; the cost of raw material consumed represented 37.01%, 43.26%, 44.29% and 47.10% of total revenues in the period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively. Conversion is done in-house at two manufacturing units (Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu and IMT Manesar, Haryana) using UV machines, dome machines, filling machines, label printing machines, shrink tunnels, pre-tape masking paper machines, masker roller machines, die-punching machines and cone high-lift pallet trucks, with an in-house testing laboratory and an R&D team; the Company states it is among the few with in-line doming application units. Outbound, the Company states it operates a Kanban / Just-in-Time inventory system to minimise stock levels, and reaches market through a dual-segment route: direct long-term B2B supply to automotive OEMs, and distributors, e-commerce platforms and direct sales for the B2C/B2B refinish market.

overview.business_model: Two streams. The manufacturing division produces adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes and printing solutions, domes and graphics, and a range of car care products, made at Unit I (SIPCOT Industrial Park, Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu) and Unit II (IMT Manesar, Haryana) under ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certifications, with customisation offered to clients. The trading segment resells electrical and pneumatic tools, abrasive sheets, discs and rolls, body shop consumables, retail products and accessories, and aerosol products. Customers are automotive OEMs and the aftermarket/refinish trade: the DRHP states that sales to Automotive Industry suppliers accounted for 100% in each of Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 and the period ended September 30, 2025, and that top-10 customers contributed 52.67%, 46.43%, 43.92% and 44.35% of total sales in the period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively. concerns_observed: FY25 cash generation does not follow the reported profit: cash flow from operations of ₹69.98 lakhs against restated PAT of ₹999.32 lakhs, i.e. 7.0% conversion by my arithmetic, after an inventory build of ₹590.56 lakhs, a receivables build of ₹418.48 lakhs and income tax paid of ₹361.77 lakhs.

The gap is not a single-year event: cumulative CFO of ₹779.93 lakhs over FY23-FY25 against cumulative restated PAT of ₹2,207.78 lakhs is 35.3% conversion, both totals my addition from the printed CFO figures of ₹330.51, ₹379.44 and ₹69.98 lakhs.

The working-capital cycle lengthens in every period: debtor days 34 to 38 to 41 to 49, inventory days 56 to 61 to 64 to 72, while creditor days move 18 to 18 to 16 to 20, so the funding is coming from the Company rather than from suppliers.

End-market diversification is nil by the issuer's own disclosure — Automotive Industry suppliers at 100% of sales in FY23, FY24, FY25 and H1FY26 — and the customer set is both concentrated and uncontracted: top-1 8.95% / 11.29% / 8.97% / 13.75%, top-5 31.38% / 32.36% / 32.48% / 39.10%, top-10 44.35% / 43.92% / 46.43% / 52.67%, with the DRHP stating 'We do not have firm commitment agreements with our customers, meaning they are not contractually obligated to purchase from us.'

Import dependence jumped in the stub period: imported raw material was 65.97% / 65.45% / 66.20% of consumption in FY23-FY25 and 84.92% at September 30, 2025 (Annexure XLIII: imported ₹2,254.69 lakhs against indigenous ₹400.36 lakhs), sourced from twelve countries, with foreign-currency expenditure of ₹5,956.69 / ₹6,460.75 / ₹7,392.58 lakhs in FY23-FY25 and ₹3,727.99 lakhs in H1FY26.

Currency movement runs through reported profit rather than sitting in a hedge: 'Gain on translation of foreign currency' of ₹33.47, ₹58.14, ₹91.03 and ₹23.54 lakhs is classified by the DRHP's own Other Income annexure as Non-Recurring, and the FY25 gain of ₹91.03 lakhs is 9.1% of FY25 PAT of ₹999.32 lakhs by my arithmetic.

The H1FY26 restatement moves profit the opposite way to all three prior years: audited PAT of ₹526.02 lakhs is restated up to ₹580.02 lakhs, a ₹54.00 lakh increase by my subtraction, driven by a Prior Period Income/Expense line of ₹105.92 lakhs (18.3% of the restated half-year PAT by my arithmetic), whereas FY23, FY24 and FY25 were restated down from ₹499.20 to ₹464.44, ₹754.88 to ₹744.02 and ₹1,010.00 to ₹999.32 lakhs.

The restatement notes describe a broad set of recognition failures rather than one adjustment: incorrect useful life on assets, gratuity recognised on an estimated basis, leave encashment on a payment basis, rent not recognised per AS 19 (₹23.66 / ₹26.62 / ₹29.44 lakh adjustments), interest on statutory dues not recognised (₹7.43 / ₹3.24 / ₹4.22 lakhs), and expenses across carriage, professional fees, repairs, software and office costs recognised in a later year as prior-period items.

'Discount received' in Other Income rises from ₹0.76 lakhs for the whole of FY25 to ₹29.82 lakhs in the six months to September 30, 2025, and the annexure labels it 'not related to business activity'.

Utilisation across the eight Chartered Engineer-certified lines (certificate dated March 15, 2026) is dispersed and unstable: in H1FY26 it runs from 5% (Unit II Die cut - Trading, down from 66% / 99% / 72%) to 135% (Unit I Die cut - Trading, up from 46% / 49% / 99%), with Unit II Polish at 27% (from 90% / 93% / 40%) and Unit I Die cut - Production printing 0% in FY23 and FY24, 3% in FY25 and 58% in H1FY26.

Both IPO-funded construction objects, ₹2,151.02 lakhs in total by my addition of ₹488.68 and ₹1,662.34 lakhs, rest on two quotations from a single contractor, M/s Royal Construction (GSTIN 08DOQPK6757F1ZB, Bhiwadi), dated 18/03/2026 and 23/03/2026 with 6-month validity, with no order disclosed as placed; the DRHP itself states 'there can be no assurance that the same vendors would be engaged'.

The quotations cover civil, PEB and external works only — no plant and machinery head appears in the Objects at all — so the two proposed units are funded to shell stage by the Offer while the equipment to run them is not costed in the Objects table.

The Objects have not been appraised: the DRHP states funding requirements rest on management, internal and third-party agency estimates and have not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency, and deployment is entirely at the Company's discretion.

verdict.our_read: Sumax Engineering Limited is a 1994-incorporated, Secunderabad-headquartered converter and trader of automotive adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, domes and graphics and car-care products, with a bought-in trading line of tools, abrasives, body-shop consumables and aerosols, made at two units at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu) and IMT Manesar (Haryana) under ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018. All figures in the DRHP are printed '(Rs In Lakhs)'. Scale is small: revenue from operations of ₹12,682.09, ₹13,079.45 and ₹14,612.60 lakhs in FY23, FY24 and FY25 (FY25 = ₹146.13 crore) and ₹7,174.69 lakhs in H1FY26, with EBITDA margin climbing 6.32% to 8.84% to 10.21% to 11.80% and restated PAT of ₹464.44, ₹744.02, ₹999.32 and ₹580.02 lakhs (FY25 PAT = ₹9.99 crore). The revenue base is undiversified by end-market — the DRHP states sales to Automotive Industry suppliers were 100% in each of FY23, FY24, FY25 and the period ended September 30, 2025 — with top-10 customers at 44.35%, 43.92%, 46.43% and 52.67% and no firm-commitment agreements with any of them, and adhesive tapes and die-cuts at 45.00% of the H1FY26 mix. Inputs are the mirror image: raw material consumed was 47.10%, 44.29%, 43.26% and 37.01% of total revenues, and Annexure XLIII shows the imported share of consumption rising 65.97% / 65.45% / 66.20% / 84.92%, sourced across twelve countries, with foreign-currency expenditure of ₹3,727.99 lakhs in H1FY26 alone. Returns look high on a thin asset base (RoCE 19.70% / 23.32% / 24.63%, RoNW 14.75% / 19.11% / 20.42%, net fixed assets of only ₹698.13 lakhs against FY25 revenue), but FY25 cash flow from operations was ₹69.98 lakhs against that ₹999.32 lakh PAT, after an inventory build of ₹590.56 lakhs, a receivables build of ₹418.48 lakhs and income tax paid of ₹361.77 lakhs.
